  - region "Simple English explanation of Vertical-Line Test":
    - paragraph: In simple English
    - heading "Understand Vertical-Line Test" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "The vertical-line test says a graph is a function of x only when every vertical line meets it in at most one point. y=x^2 passes; x^2+y^2=1 fails because x=0 hits (0,1) and (0,−1). A useful rule is Function test: one x -> one y. You can learn Vertical-Line Test by trying one small example instead of long theory."
    - paragraph: "Sweep a vertical line across the graph. Count hits. More than one hit means it is not a function of x. Example: Does a circle pass the vertical-line test? Draw a vertical line through the circle. It crosses twice for some x-values. So the answer is No."
    - paragraph: "In real life, map paths: One x-position may have two heights. Watch out: Using a horizontal line to test if it is a function. Use vertical lines for functions of x."
    - complementary:
      - generic: Try this example
      - paragraph: Does a circle pass the vertical-line test?
      - generic "Compare your answer"
